To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

actinomycin-D treatment of mice results in glycogen depletion, decreased glycogen-synthase activity, and the solubiliza-tion of phosphorylase, and that these effects are reversed by glucose administration but not by cortisol administration.

actinomycin-D administration caused glycogen depletion, decrease of glycogen synthetases, solubilization and activation of phosphorylase, decrease in UDP-glucosyltransferase and phosphoglyceromutase activities, and no effect on the activities of glucose 6-phophatase, glucose 6-phospate dehydrogenas, pyruvat kinase, and UDP-glucuronate dehydrogenases.
actinomycin-D administration to starved mice produces a marked decrease in glycogen and in the activity of the glycogen-synthase enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of actinomycind on the metabolism of liver glycogen.
the effects of glucocorticoid and glucose stimulation on the synthesis and breakdown of liver glycogen.
the effects of glucocorticoids on liver metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
actinomycin inhibits cortisol action in liver by interfering with the synthesis of a specific protein(s).
the effects of actionycin D on liver phosphorylase are not due to a direct action on the enzyme but rather to a secondary action on the hormonal regulation of the enzyme.
the administration of actinomycine D to starved animals causes a marked glycogenolysis, which is not reversed by glucose ingestion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the administration of actinomycine D inhibits glycogenesis in mouse livers by preventing the action of the glucocorticoids on the synthesis of a protein factor that is required for glycogen synthesis and that this protein factor is probably a regulatory protein that controls the activity of glycogen synthetases and phosphorylase.
the effect of cortisol is to increase the synthesis of glycogen, whereas that of glucose is to increase the degradation of glycogen.

the administration of cortisol to starved mice produces an increase in liver-glycogen content and in glycogen-syn- thetase activity and a shift of phosphorylase from the particulate to the supernatant fraction, whereas the administration of glucose does not affect the glycogen content but causes a shift of glycogen synthetases from the supernatant to the particulate fraction, and the administration of both cortisol and glucose to starved mice causes an increase in liverglycogen
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of actinomycins as antibiotics in human medicine is not justified by the results of this study.

we have shown that a single dose of actinomycins can have a significant effect on the activity of a specific protein, in this case a specific protein that is involved in the metabolism of glucose and insulin.
the actinomycin-D-induced inhibition of the glucocorticoid-induced increase in liver glycogenic activity is not a general phenomenon, but is specific for the glucocorticoids.
